summary: Unit-restriction and arithmetic-numerator checkpoint: preserves all 25 predecessor nodes and adds 20 declaration-sized nodes for the rational smoothing average, bounded psi-invariance proof plan, the unit Euler factor and the inverse-weighted integral numerator, with exact imported operator and inverseWeight/inverseMahler interfaces. Two precise generic averaging requests remain at PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2 and propagate to the numerical unit/numerator moment statements. The arithmetic constructions, support, primitive equation, uniqueness and Amice comparison use existing exact supplier nodes. No stage or implementation is closed; regularity, pseudomeasure division, parameter independence and later layers remain explicit obligations. Six arithmetic relation nodes now give the smoothing cocycle, cross-smoothing and reflection correction for μ_a, and the scalar-free cocycle, cross-smoothing and evenness for the existing inverse-weighted numerator. Their proof chains avoid both open averaging requests; completed-algebra comparisons, regularity and pseudomeasure independence remain gaps.

nodes.title: Binomial smoothing denominator
nodes.statement: Define q_a in R[[T]] by coefficient_n(q_a)=choose(a,n+1). It is the integral quotient of (1+T)^a−1 by T. The definition is coefficient-wise and does not invert T.
hypotheses: R is a commutative ring; a is a natural number. Write q_a(T)=∑ choose(a,n+1)Tⁿ and b_a(T)=∑ choose(a,n+2)Tⁿ. All binomial coefficients are cast from ℕ to R.
proofSteps: Apply the existing PowerSeries.mk to the indicated natural binomial coefficients.
The coefficient API follows from coeff_mk; n=0 gives the constant coefficient a.
The polynomial binomial formula gives Tq_a=(1+T)^a−1; coefficient maps preserve the natural coefficients.
acceptance: The coefficient definition gives a polynomial of degree at most a−1 for a>0; it gives zero when a=0. The tests distinguish the quotient by T from the unshifted binomial polynomial.
